author: Augustine of Hippo
addressee: The Catholic congregation at Caesarea in Mauretania, with Emeritus the Donatist bishop present
occasion: Emeritus, a Donatist bishop, came to the city two days earlier and agreed to enter the Catholic church. The Catholic bishops, with Deuterius the metropolitan of Caesarea presiding alongside Augustine and others, held a public session to question him about why he came and to expose the weakness of the Donatist position before the people.
argument: Augustine publicly confronts Emeritus, the Donatist bishop who has come to the Catholic church but remains silent. He argues that the Donatists were defeated at the Conference of Carthage not by power but by truth, and that their own treatment of the Maximianist schism proves their inconsistency: they received back in their honors men they had solemnly condemned, without rebaptizing them, while refusing communion with the worldwide Catholic Church over the long-settled case of Caecilian. He urges the people to see the difference between Catholic peace and heretical dissension, and calls for prayer for Emeritus's conversion.

outline.move: Augustine recounts how Emeritus came to the city and entered the church, and how he exhorted him and the people on peace and unity.
Augustine explains the purpose of the session: to question Emeritus so the people may learn the difference between Catholic peace and Donatist dissension.
Augustine asks Emeritus why he came and whether he was defeated by truth or by power; Emeritus deflects, saying the records indicate whether he was defeated or victorious.
Emeritus falls silent; Augustine urges the people to pray for him and proposes that the Conference records be read annually during Lent.
Alypius reads the Catholic bishops' letter to Marcellinus, in which they promise to surrender their sees if the Donatists prove their case, or to share them if the Donatists return.
Augustine recalls how nearly three hundred bishops eagerly accepted this offer of humility for the sake of unity.
The letter continues: bishops should lay down their dignity if it hinders the gathering of Christ's flock, and the Donatists should prefer reconciliation to rebaptizing the world.
Augustine introduces the case of the Maximianists, which he says the Donatists had no response to at the Conference.
Augustine narrates the Maximianist schism: Maximianus was condemned, his followers expelled, yet Felicianus and Praetextatus were later received back in their honors without rebaptism.
Augustine reads Emeritus's own condemnation of the Maximianists and contrasts it with the Donatists' later embrace of the condemned men.
Augustine refutes the Donatist excuse of a time limit and argues that if Felicianus did not defile Emeritus, Caecilian could not defile the world.
Augustine closes by comparing the Church to a tree seeking its broken branch and a shepherd seeking a lost sheep, and calls for prayer for Emeritus.

cast.name: Augustine
cast.who: Catholic bishop of Hippo, the main speaker.

cast.name: Emeritus
cast.who: Donatist bishop, present but largely silent; ordained by the Donatists of this city.

cast.name: Alypius
cast.who: Catholic bishop of Thagaste, who reads the letter to Marcellinus.

cast.name: Deuterius
cast.who: Catholic metropolitan bishop of Caesarea, presiding with the other bishops.

cast.name: Palladius
cast.who: Catholic bishop, present; his see is given as Tigabitanus in the source.

cast.name: Marcellinus
cast.who: Imperial tribune and notary who presided over the Conference of Carthage.

cast.name: Maximianus
cast.who: Deacon of Carthage who led a schism against the Donatist bishop Primianus.

cast.name: Primianus
cast.who: Donatist bishop of Carthage who excommunicated Maximianus.

cast.name: Felicianus
cast.who: One of the twelve condemned with Maximianus, later received back in his honors.

cast.name: Praetextatus
cast.who: One of the twelve condemned with Maximianus, later received back in his honors.

cast.name: Caecilian
cast.who: Catholic bishop of Carthage whose acquittal the Donatists refused to accept.

cast.name: Donatus
cast.who: Founder of the Donatist party, condemned after Caecilian's acquittal.

cast.name: Optatus
cast.who: Called 'the Gildonian' in the source; through him Felicianus and Praetextatus were restored.

cast.name: Rogatus
cast.who: Bishop ordained in Praetextatus's place, later a Catholic, mutilated by Circumcellions.

voices.speaker: Alypius (reading the bishops' letter)
voices.how_marked: Narrative introduction: 'Alypius episcopus ecclesiae catholicae epistulam recitauit' and 'Item legit'

voices.speaker: Augustine (interrupting the reading with commentary)
voices.how_marked: Narrative markers: 'Et cum legeret, Augustinus episcopus dixit' and 'cumque recitaret, Augustinus episcopus dixit'

voices.speaker: Emeritus (quoted in his own condemnation of the Maximianists)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by Augustine as Emeritus's own words: 'uerba ipsius sunt', 'ab isto Emerito est dicta sententia'

key_terms.sense: The formal public debate between Catholic and Donatist bishops held at Carthage in 411.
The Donatist party or communion, named after Donatus.
Full fellowship in the Catholic Church, especially sharing the Eucharist.
The visible unity of the Catholic Church throughout the world.
The peace of the Catholic Church, contrasted with Donatist dissension.
A split or division in the Church, especially the Maximianist break from the Donatists.
The Donatist practice of baptizing again those who came to them from the Catholic Church.
Followers of Maximianus, who split from the Donatists and were condemned by them.
Violent Donatist bands known for attacks on Catholics and on their own opponents.
The imperial official, Marcellinus, appointed to judge the Conference of Carthage.
The office and dignity of a bishop.
The bosom or embrace of the Catholic Church, into which former Donatists are received.
One who holds a false doctrine and is outside the true Church, as the Donatists regarded the Maximianists.
The time limit the Donatists claimed they gave the Maximianists to return before final condemnation.

scripture: The author cites the Old Testament in Latin versions based on the Septuagint, using names such as Dathan, Chore and Abiron (Dathan, Korah and Abiram). Psalms are cited according to the Septuagint numbering. Modern citations should use standard English Bible names and numbering, with a note where Septuagint Psalm numbers differ from the Hebrew.
uncertain: The exact date of the session beyond the consular year (418) and the day (twelfth day before the Kalends of October, i.e. September 20).
Whether Emeritus ever spoke beyond his brief replies recorded in section 3.
The precise identity of all twelve bishops condemned with Maximianus.
Whether the 'Rogatus' mentioned in section 9 is the same as the Rogatus who was later a Catholic bishop.
The exact see of Palladius, given in the source only as 'Tigabitano'.
Whether Emeritus's own see was Caesarea; the source says he was ordained by the Donatists of this city but does not explicitly name his see.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Emeritus, a Donatist bishop, came to the city two days earlier and agreed to enter the Catholic church.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: quando uenit ad hanc ciuitatem die nudiustertiana frater noster Emeritus Donatistarum adhuc episcopus... at ille nobis sine ulla recusatione consensit; ubi nos putauimus eum ita communionem catholicam non recusaturum, quemadmodum uel spontaneum obtulit aduentum uel ad ecclesiam uenire minime dubitauit. illo autem in peruersitate haeretica quamuis intra ecclesiam catholicam diutius remorante
_unresolved_facts.fix: Emeritus came to the city two days earlier and agreed to come to the Catholic church building, but he did not agree to enter Catholic communion; he remained in heretical perversity despite being inside the Catholic church.

_unresolved_facts.claim: with Deuterius the metropolitan of Caesarea presiding alongside Augustine and others
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: cum Deuterius episcopus metropolitanus Caesariensis una cum Alypio Tagastensi, Augustino Hipponiensi, Possidio Calamensi, Rustico Cartenitano, Palladio Tigabitano et ceteris episcopis in exedram processissent
_unresolved_facts.fix: Deuterius was present as metropolitan bishop, but the source does not indicate he was 'presiding' in any formal sense distinct from the other bishops; they all processed in together.

_unresolved_facts.claim: they received back in their honors men they had solemnly condemned, without rebaptizing them
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: post annos duos aut tres per Optatum Gildonianum post multas illis illatas persecutiones iudiciariis prosecutionibus et tota acrimonia potestatum in suis honoribus susceperunt
_unresolved_facts.fix: they received back in their honors men they had solemnly condemned, without rebaptizing them, after two or three years, after many persecutions inflicted on them, through judicial prosecutions and the full harshness of authorities

_unresolved_facts.claim: Augustine asks Emeritus why he came and whether he was defeated by truth or by power; Emeritus deflects, saying the records indicate whether he was defeated or victorious.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Emeritus episcopus partis Donati dixit: Gesta indicant si uictus sum aut uici, si ueritate uictus sum aut potestate oppressus sum. Augustinus episcopus ecclesiae catholicae dixit: Quare ergo uenisti? Emeritus episcopus partis Donati dixit: Ut hoc dicerem quod requiris. Augustinus episcopus ecclesiae catholicae dixit: Requiro quare ueneris. hoc non quaererem, si non uenisses. Emeritus episcopus partis Donati dixit notario qui excipiebat: Fac.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Emeritus does not merely deflect; he explicitly says 'The records indicate whether I was defeated or victorious, whether I was defeated by truth or oppressed by power,' then when pressed again on why he came, he says 'To say what you ask' and then, when pressed a third time, tells the notary 'Do it' (i.e., record his silence or the proceedings).

_unresolved_facts.claim: Emeritus falls silent; Augustine urges the people to pray for him and proposes that the Conference records be read annually during Lent.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Sed si omnia gesta uobis legere uelimus... ut annis omnibus per ieiuniorum dies, id est quadragesima ante pascha... eadem gesta collationis per annos singulos uniuersa a capite in finem recitentur ex ordine
_unresolved_facts.fix: Augustine urges the people to pray for Emeritus's repentance and not to follow his perdition; the proposal to read Conference records annually during Lent is presented as something already done at Carthage, Thagaste, Constantina, and Hippo, and that Deuterius should continue doing at Caesarea, not as a new proposal.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Augustine reads Emeritus's own condemnation of the Maximianists
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ab isto Emerito est dicta sententia ubi illi damnati sunt. legatur ipsa sententia
_unresolved_facts.fix: Augustine asks that Emeritus's sentence be read aloud by someone else (legatur), not that he reads it himself; the text is introduced as having been dictated by Emeritus (dictante prolata, 'dictated by him').

_unresolved_facts.claim: Optatus... Called 'the Gildonian' in the source; through him Felicianus and Praetextatus were restored.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: per Optatum Gildonianum post multas illis illatas persecutiones iudiciariis prosecutionibus et tota acrimonia potestatum in suis honoribus susceperunt
_unresolved_facts.fix: Optatus 'the Gildonian' acted after many persecutions had been inflicted on them, through judicial prosecutions and the full harshness of authorities; the source does not say he alone restored them but that they were received back through these means.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Alypius episcopus ecclesiae catholicae epistulam recitauit
_unresolved_facts.fix: Alypius reads the letter in section 5; section 7 contains Augustine's commentary on the letter ('Et cum legeret, Augustinus episcopus dixit' and 'cumque recitaret, Augustinus episcopus dixit'), not Alypius's continued reading. The voice in section 7 is primarily Augustine interrupting, not Alypius reading.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Emeritus (quoted in his own condemnation of the Maximianists)... sections ["10"]
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ab isto Emerito est dicta sententia... legatur ipsa sententia
_unresolved_facts.fix: The voice in section 10 is Augustine quoting/paraphrasing what Emeritus dictated, not Emeritus speaking directly in the present proceedings. Augustine introduces it as 'words of this man' and 'he dictated' (dictante prolata), but the actual recitation is performed by a reader at Augustine's request, not by Emeritus himself.
